concept.name: Correction
concept.definition: A counter-trend decline within a prevailing uptrend, conventionally defined at the index level as a fall of 10% or more from the recent peak (but less than the 20% associated with a bear market). It is a descriptive, magnitude-based label applied to price action, not a forecast of what follows.
concept.intuition: The market takes a meaningful step back inside a larger climb — deeper than a pullback, but short of a bear market.
concept.mechanics: Measured as the percentage decline from the recent high: a drop of roughly 10% earns the label 'correction' by market convention; corrections are typically shorter in duration than bear markets and, in an intact bull trend, are followed by recovery to new highs.
concept.formula: Correction depth (%) = (peak price - trough price) / peak price x 100; >= 10% is the conventional correction threshold, >= 20% the conventional bear market threshold.
concept.failure_modes: The 10% threshold is arbitrary, and a correction can always deepen into a bear market; buying 'the correction' fails when the decline keeps going.
concept.misconceptions: That a correction 'must' end near 10%; the label is retrospective, and nothing bounds the eventual depth at the time it is occurring.
concept.example: The 2023-2024 bull market saw several ~10% declines (banking stress, AI concerns) that each recovered to new highs — textbook corrections within an uptrend.

citations.source: Real Investment Advice — A Bear Market Rally? Or, Just A Correction?
